narrative: The model estimated a 38% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean repayment problems are certain; it means your estimated risk is above the bank’s acceptable cutoff, so the application was denied. The strongest influence on the decision was your savings profile, and it actually counted in your favour. The second most important factor was your checking-account status: being below zero pushed the decision toward bad credit. This matters because only 12.6% of approved applicants had an overdrawn checking account, while 59.2% had no overdraft. The third factor, the furniture/equipment purpose of the loan, also slightly favoured approval, but it was weaker than the checking-account concern. Other cautionary signals include a requested term of 24 months versus about 19 months for approved applicants and an amount of 7,721 DM versus an average of about 3,020 DM. To improve your position, ask the bank for the specific decline reasons, bring the checking account into credit if possible, provide evidence of savings or stable income, and consider a smaller or shorter loan or adding a guarantor. Reapplying without changing these points is unlikely to produce a different outcome.
